close_reason: Substantially completed by commit 0ae115e (docs(clients): add # Errors rustdoc sections to all public method builders) which added # Errors sections to every public async method builder across all 7 *-client crates including jmap-chat-client. Every method the bead's description specifically called out (blob_lookup, chat_changes, chat_create, message_update, space_update, push_subscription_create, push_subscription_update) now has a # Errors section. The one remaining fallible public method, SessionClient::chat_account_id in methods/mod.rs, was a sync accessor whose error case was already described in inline prose; the follow-up commit on this bead lifts it to a formal # Errors section for consistency.
description:
Files: crate-jmap-chat-client/src/methods/*.rs — every method on `SessionClient` returning `Result<_, ClientError>`.

`ClientError` (re-exported from `jmap-base-client`) is `#[non_exhaustive]` and has at least 15 variants. Callers writing defensive error handling cannot determine from the function signature or rustdoc which variants are possible. Examples of the gap:

- `blob_lookup` (blob.rs:144) — can return `InvalidArgument` (empty blob_ids), `InvalidSession` (no chat primary account), `Parse`, plus transport variants from `call_internal`. None listed in the doc.
- `chat_changes` (chat.rs:90) — returns `InvalidArgument` on empty `since_state`, plus the usual. Not listed.
- `chat_create` (chat.rs:180) — returns `InvalidArgument` for empty `name` in Group/Channel variants (lines 205-209, 233-237) and `Parse` from internal serialization. Not listed.
- `message_update` (message.rs:215) — returns `InvalidArgument` when `sender_reaction_id` is empty or contains '/' or '~' (lines 253-263, 271-281); returns `Parse` from `body_type` / `read_disposition` serialization. Not listed.
- `space_update` (space.rs:239) — returns `InvalidArgument` for several empty-string conditions (channel name, role name, category name) plus `Parse` from many serialization sites. None listed.
- `push_subscription_create` (misc.rs:201) — returns `InvalidArgument` for empty `device_client_id`, empty `url`, and duplicate accountIds in `chat_push`; returns `Parse` from `ChatPushConfig` serialization. None listed.
- `push_subscription_update` (misc.rs:282) — partial: lists `InvalidArgument` for empty id and mutual-exclusion conditions; missing duplicate-accountId and Parse.

A few methods DO partially enumerate: `message_create` documents `RateLimited`, `chat_capability` describes three-state output, `quota_get/changes` lists `InvalidSession` and `InvalidArgument`. These are the exceptions.

Pattern fix: add an `# Errors` section to every fallible public method. Standard Rust rustdoc convention. Each section should list the `ClientError::*` variants the method can produce and under what conditions, distinguishing between:
- pre-network defensive guards that fire on caller error (these are programming-error variants)
- spec-precondition failures returned by the server
- network/transport errors that always exist for any JMAP call

Approximate scope: 44 methods across 8 method files. Per-method work is small (3-6 lines of doc each) but coordinated — a propagation epic with one child per file is the natural shape.

Caller impact today: any caller writing `match err { ClientError::RateLimited{..} => retry, _ => bubble }` has no API contract telling them what other variants exist. They will either pattern-match conservatively (`_ =>` bubble) and miss legitimate retry opportunities, or pattern-match defensively and have to revisit every match site whenever a new variant is added.
title: 44 fallible public methods lack # Errors doc sections
